t + 3 sAct 1 · the column climbs

It leaves the vent as one thing, not three hundred

The old column was three THREE.Points clouds — 760 untextured dots in a 15 m cylinder. A points material with no texture draws a hard square, so at any distance you could count them, and the scatter left altitude bands empty. That is both halves of your complaint: separate rocks, and several circular clouds. It is opaque overlapping billows now, the same primitive the pyroclastic flow already used.

t + 14 sAct 2 · sustained

The eruption is 36 seconds, and this is the middle of it

Your St Helens frame set the shape: a narrow incandescent throat, a stem, and an umbrella several times wider than the stem spreading downwind — pale grey, not brown. Altitude is now derived from a wrapping phase rather than tracked per billow, because the first attempt drained the middle of the column and left a glowing lump at the vent and a grey lump in the sky with nothing between them.

t + 30 sAct 3 · the ash-out

The world goes away

You were right that filling the map is both easier and better. What actually happens to a town under a collapsing column is not that it gets hit by an object — it is that you cannot see the mountain, the street, or the person in front of you. As geometry that is a dome nobody can render; as the scene's own fog it is four numbers that work at every distance. 300 m of visibility collapses to 34. Note the direction: brighter, not darker — inside fine ash you are in a luminous grey nothing, so the sun goes out and the ambient comes up. On the left, at the same second, the old eruption has been over for ten seconds and a meteor shower is already queuing.

t + 9 sThe flow

A black plate with glowing cracks in it

This is the correction your Fagradalsfjall photograph made, and it is not a tuning change — a flow is not a dark ribbon with a bright stripe painted down it. It is a near-black crusted plate broken into slabs, with the incandescence showing through a network of seams that pinch shut where two slabs have welded and gape where the plate has torn, plus one small very bright throat at the vent. So the second mesh stopped being a channel and became five seams that pinch on their own hash. Eight thin rivulets now instead of four fat ribbons, the way your Arenal frame fans them off one summit.

t + 41 sAfter the event

It turns black and hardens, and it stays

The payoff for making the flow slow. A creeping flow that has only made a third of the cone when the timer runs out used to be deleted — a worse lie than the speed was. It freezes where it stood, the cracks close, the glow goes out over about nine seconds, and eight black basalt tongues stay on the mountain for the rest of the match. Cold rock stops hit-testing: it is terrain now, not a hazard.

Also in this pass

  • Lava burns instead of instakilling — half a second costs 44 HP, about 1.2 s kills, so stepping out of something slower than a walk actually saves you.
  • The pyroclastic cloud you see is the cloud that kills you: one lane function now serves the geometry and the hit test, and it takes height, so a 25 m surge stops killing people standing above it.
  • A volcanic death no longer plays nukefx's nuclear double-pulse whiteout. It gets an ember-to-ash sear instead — orange in, black out.
  • Gates: MATHGATE ok · volcano-check 24/24.
